subhead: Take a free practice quiz or get instant, explained answers to SERE 100.2 Code of Conduct questions — survival, evasion, resistance, and escape fundamentals, without the guesswork.
metaTitle: SERE 100.2 Training Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free SERE 100.2 Level A Code of Conduct quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Code of Conduct articles, survival priorities, and more.
whyItWorks: SERE 100.2 leans heavily on the six Articles of the Code of Conduct and specific survival/evasion priorities, which are easy to blur together across a long course. Cambo reads the exact question and gives you the specific article or principle that applies, not just a general answer.

sampleQuestions.q: Which Article of the Code of Conduct addresses a service member's duty to keep faith with fellow prisoners?
sampleQuestions.a: Article IV — it requires service members to keep faith with fellow prisoners, help them, and give no information or take part in actions harmful to them.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the first priority in a survival situation, according to SERE training?
sampleQuestions.a: Protection — assessing and addressing immediate threats to life (medical, environmental) before moving on to water, fire, food, and signaling.

sampleQuestions.q: Which Article of the Code of Conduct establishes a service member's duty to resist to the utmost of their ability if captured?
sampleQuestions.a: Article II — a service member will never surrender their forces while they have the means to resist, and if in command, will never surrender members of their command while they still can resist.

sampleQuestions.q: In a survival situation, why does SERE training place "protection" before "water" in priority order?
sampleQuestions.a: Because immediate threats to life — exposure, injury, environmental hazards — can kill much faster than dehydration, so stabilizing those risks comes first.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the general guidance under the Code of Conduct regarding providing information to a captor?
sampleQuestions.a: Give only name, rank, service number, and date of birth — the "Big Four" — and resist providing further information to the best of your ability.

sampleQuestions.q: What does Article VI of the Code of Conduct establish?
sampleQuestions.a: That a service member will never forget they are an American, responsible for their actions, and will trust in their country and its way of life — the article covering enduring loyalty and faith.

faqs.q: How long does SERE 100.2 take to complete?
faqs.a: Around 3-4 hours, and it typically needs to be completed in a single sitting on the JKO platform.
Service members and DoD civilians with a moderate risk of isolation, captivity, or hostage detention, often as a pre-deployment requirement.

faqs.q: What's the difference between SERE 100.1 and 100.2?
faqs.a: SERE 100.1 is the civilian-oriented version. SERE 100.2 Level A is the military version, covering the same core Code of Conduct principles in more depth for service members.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD or JKO?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Department of Defense or Joint Knowledge Online.

faqs.q: How many Articles are in the Code of Conduct?
faqs.a: Six — covering topics from a service member's duty to resist the enemy, to keeping faith with fellow prisoners, to remaining loyal to country and chain of command.
Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape — the four core skill areas covered by the training.
